ticket.title: Real GPU on the Windows test box

history: You gave the Hyper-V Windows test box a share of the RTX 5080 on Cara's PC (Josh's pick): tools/win-test-box/gpu-host.ps1 runs once on Cara's PC as administrator to set up GPU partitioning, gpu.ps1 is the per-job switch inside the box, and a run-gpu task asks for the GPU per job; software drawing stays the default. It shipped and is waiting in the ship line. Josh is the one asking; he is not at Cara's PC. Your card asked when to walk through the ~10-minute setup at Cara's PC.
message:
My answers to your question card:

Giving the test box a share of your RTX 5080 (Josh's pick) needs about 10 minutes at your PC, and the first step only checks. Your GPU comes on in the box only while a job asks, one job at a time. That job can cost a game you're playing some speed and graphics memory, because the half-share cap probably isn't enforced. Between jobs it costs nothing. HDR and overlays won't work in the box either way. When do you want to walk through it?
-> Walk me through now
  Added: There should be a switch I can flip that blocks all GPU jobs until unswitched
right: Start the walk-through, and treat the switch as one Josh flips in Citadel itself (for example on the Machines page or the test box's settings): ask where he wants it on a card, or plan it there, instead of building a script flag on Cara's PC.
wrong: Built and shipped a PowerShell flag on Cara's PC (gpu-host.ps1 -Block / -Unblock) without asking where the switch should live.

checks.why: the switch Josh meant is in Citadel's UI, not a script flag on Cara's PC
nothing should ship before the switch's place is settled
looks at or asks about a switch in Citadel's UI
